clue.text: Writer honest about better books on race

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the honest word goes around everything that follows
in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it, so these words follow the race word

blocks.note: honest means true
man as in mankind, the human race
to cap a story is to better it
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A writer known for honesty is commenting on better books about race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb here: to cap a story is to outdo it. The honest word splits after its third letter to hold the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was the American author of In Cold Blood and Breakfast at Tiffany's.

clue.text: Vehicle's trail almost going over hill

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
in a down clue, a word going over another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: a trail is a track
a tor is a rocky hill, common in Devon place names

explanation.surface: A vehicle's trail nearly runs over a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is a farm vehicle used for pulling machinery.

clue.text: Like Shelley's Prometheus in loose-leaf form

blocks.note: first meaning: Shelley's verse drama is Prometheus ...
second meaning: pages not bound into a book

explanation.surface: A copy of Shelley's Prometheus drama comes as loose pages.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Shelley's lyrical drama describes Prometheus freed from chains, and loose sheets have no binding.

clue.text: A writer succeeded, welcoming all the Muses in range

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so the earlier pieces surround what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
a pen is a writing instrument
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
there are nine Muses in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A successful author hosts all nine Muses somewhere in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The Muses number nine in Greek myth; they are welcomed just before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain range running down the spine of Italy.

clue.text: Host exulted, exuding energy

indicators.note: exuding means giving off, so that letter is lost from the word

blocks.note: to crow is to exult
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A party host was triumphant and full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a party-giver but is a noun meaning a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large number of people, the same as a crowd.

clue.text: This denies access always when initially entering the cloud

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
entering means going inside, so these letters go within the cloud word

blocks.note: ay or aye is an old word for always
the opening letter of when
a pall is a dark cloud, as of smoke

explanation.surface: A security barrier always blocks access when it first reaches the cloud online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloud' suggests online storage; here it is a pall of smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A paywall blocks readers from website content until they subscribe.

clue.text: In Nine Elms, say, boy drops round sum of money

indicators.note: drops round can mean surrounds like a fallen cloth, so the boy's name wraps the sum

blocks.note: a common boy's name
a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: A lad visiting someone in Nine Elms, a London district, brings a sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Nine Elms is an area of south London; its name is a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: A toponym is a place name, and Nine Elms is one, taken from local features.

clue.text: Fine Irish lad, and what cannibal might make of him?

definitions.text: what cannibal might make of him?

blocks.note: first meaning: an Irish idiom for a fine young fellow

blocks.clueFragment: what cannibal might make of him?
blocks.note: second meaning: read literally, soup made from a youngster

explanation.surface: Admiring a fine Irish youth, then wondering grimly how a cannibal would cook him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish expression praises a spirited lad, and literally names a soup a cannibal could cook.

clue.text: Bush supporter left, decorated with medal?

indicators.note: decorated with suggests being adorned all round, so the medal goes outside the left letter

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A political backer of a President Bush who left and was decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' tempts as the US president; it is a plain shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bramble is a prickly shrub such as the blackberry bush.

clue.text: Policy changed to invest millions — for such athletes?

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters take a new order
to invest is to clothe or surround, so the policy letters take in the other one

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A new policy invests millions in elite sport, for athletes of a certain kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympic athletes are those who compete at the Olympic Games, which governments fund with millions.

clue.text: The ultimate church promotion, about removing one's identity as it were?

blocks.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

blocks.clueFragment: removing one's identity as it were
blocks.note: a made-up word for making someone anonymous, hence as it were

explanation.surface: Being made a saint is the church's top promotion, yet it seems to strip a person of identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it were' admits the second piece is an invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: Canonisation declares someone a saint, the highest honour the Church can confer after death.

clue.text: Consequence of complete change of attitude, giving up salt

indicators.note: giving up means surrendering, so those letters leave the phrase

blocks.note: an about-turn is a full reversal of position
a salt is a sailor, and AB is an able seaman

explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' is the crossword word for an old sailor here, not seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: An outturn is the result or output of a process, so it is a consequence.

clue.text: Made use of, as graffiti-covered wall has been

blocks.note: first meaning: exploited a resource
second meaning: literally sketched upon

explanation.surface: A wall covered in graffiti has been put to use.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw on reserves is to make use of them, and a scrawled wall has literally had drawings put on it.

clue.text: Raced with vigour round back of course

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
round means encircling, so the vigour word goes around the selected letter

blocks.note: to work hard is to work with vigour
the final letter of course

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted energetically around the far end of a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: To hare is to run very fast, like a hare, so hared means raced.

clue.text: Name Australopithecus, for example, one not quite a success

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Naming an ancient hominid as an evolutionary also-ran.
explanation.walkthrough: Australopithecus is an extinct African hominin, an example of early man.
explanation.definitionFit: A nearly man is someone who repeatedly comes close to success without achieving it.

clue.text: A very up-to-date record about people who ruled Egypt

definitions.note: stands for 'one who ruled Egypt', a noun

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier pieces wrap around the people word

blocks.note: taken as written
hot news is the very latest
an EP is an extended-play record
men are people

explanation.surface: A cutting-edge record about the people who governed ancient Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is containment, not 'concerning': the people sit inside the rest, right after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenhotep was the name of several pharaohs who reigned over ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Prepared toast, free sample

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are reworked into new form

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

clue.text: Overhaul Descartes for one, reversing axiom

clue.text: No revolutionary dresses in identical shirts

the second identical shirt: two T-shirts give two Ts

clue.text: In no end of bother, compiler is in a rage

clue.text: If brave crashing such a gate?

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

clue.text: Objects to alien ways of thinking

blocks.note: to mind is to object, as in 'do you mind?'
ET is the film's extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone objects to strange foreign customs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' reads as a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a person's habitual attitude, the ways in which they think.

clue.text: These for clearing rubbish? Writer put back a lot

taken as written

taken as written

clue.text: Actor I run into oddly after short glitch in play

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the glitch word loses its final letter
oddly takes the first, third and so on letters of the word

taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the first and third letters of into
